newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices end up on rebound.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices end up on rebound.

text.p: China's B share indices ended up on Friday in line with sharp rebounds on the A share market, but most investors remained on the sidelines as most listed companies have yet to release 1996 results, brokers said.
Shanghai's B index rose 1.12 percent to 70.12 points on turnover of $6.2 million against $7.1 million on Thursday.
Shenzhen's B index gained 1.3 percent to close at 164.25 points on thin turnover of HK$81.5 million ($10.5 million), compared with Thursday's HK$104.2 million.
Brokers said the A shares jump late in the session sparked buying by domestic investors on the B share markets and reversed the morning's losses.

"Trading by domestic investors is the main factor behind the movements on the B share market at the moment, with overseas investors staying on the sidelines for the company reporting season," one Shanghai broker said.
"The day's trading volume was thin despite the rise, indicating that the potential for a further rise is small in the absence of fresh capital," a second broker said.
On the Shanghai B market, Shanghai Dazhong Taxi Co was the star on speculative institutional buying, jumping $0.068 or 6.66 percent to $1.088 on volume of 69,000 shares.
Real estate developer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development traded most amid expectations that it will post poor 1996 results, but some domestic institutions continued to support it.
It ended flat at $0.94 on volume of 1.6 million shares.
In Shenzhen, Tsann Kuen Enterprise Co Ltd was the best performer, closing HK$0.15 or 3.66 percent higher at HK$4.25 on volume of 300,020 shares.

Meanwhile, the Shanghai and Shenzhen A share indices jumped after Thursday's falls on institutional support for selective stocks which triggered large follow-up buying late in the session, brokers said.
Shanghai's A share index jumped 4.22 percent to 1,222.436 points on volume of 699.2 million shares worth 8.4 billion yuan ($1 million), little changed from Thursday's 8.3 billion yuan.
Shanghai Wangchunhua Industrial was the star on institutional buying ahead of the close, surging 1.07 yuan to its daily 10 percent limit-up of 11.75 yuan on volume of 694,300 shares.
Shenzhen's A index gained 2.59 percent to 429.65 points on turnover of 8.73 billion yuan, compared with 9.6 billion yuan on Thursday.
